intro: Professionals and everyday users convert megapascals (MPa) to psi (psi) when working across si and imperial standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One megapascal equals 145.037738 psi, while 1 pounds per square inch equals 0.006895 megapascals. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between MPa and psi. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many psi (psi) are in 1 megapascal (MPa)?
faqs.answer: There are 145.03773773 psi (psi) in 1 megapascal (MPa), which rounds to 145.0377 psi for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pounds per square inch equals 0.006895 megapascals.

faqs.question: How do I convert megapascals to psi (MPa to psi)?
faqs.answer: To convert megapascals to psi, use the formula: psi = MPa × 145.03773773. For example, converting 10 MPa gives 1,450.3774 psi.

faqs.question: What is 10 megapascals in psi?
faqs.answer: 10 megapascals (MPa) equals exactly 1,450.3774 psi (psi) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
